guide.title: DIN rail types: 35 × 7.5, 35 × 15 and 15 mm explained
guide.description: How to choose DIN rail for terminal blocks: 35 × 7.5 vs 35 × 15 mm top-hat rail, 15 mm miniature rail, materials and ground block approvals
keyTakeaways: 35 × 7.5 mm top-hat rail fits most terminal blocks
35 × 15 mm deep rail adds strength for heavy or large components
Check that ground blocks are approved for your rail's profile and material

body.text: Almost every modular terminal block clips onto a DIN rail. The rail dimensions are standardized (EN 60715), so blocks from different manufacturers fit the same rail. The profile you choose still affects strength, depth and grounding.

head: Rail
Typical use
rows: The default for terminal blocks, relays and small devices
Deeper and stiffer, for heavier components and long unsupported spans
Small terminal blocks in compact enclosures
Older asymmetric profile, still found in legacy panels

body.caption: Feed-through, neutral (blue) and ground (green-yellow) blocks of one series all clip onto the same rail profile.

items: Zinc-plated steel is the common general-purpose choice
Aluminium is lighter but less stiff
Copper rail is used where the rail itself must carry earth current

body.text: Slotted (perforated) rail is easier to mount and lighter. Solid rail is stiffer and suits heavy loads.

If you are matching an existing panel, measure the rail height. 7.5 mm and 15 mm rail look the same from the front, but the depth changes how far every device stands off the back plate, and mixing them in one row leaves devices out of line.

body.title: Ground blocks and the rail
body.text: Ground (PE) terminal blocks bond to earth through the rail, so the manufacturer lists the rail profiles and materials each one is approved for. Check that list, and make sure the rail is bonded to the enclosure's earth.

items: Use 35 × 7.5 mm rail unless heavy devices or long unsupported spans call for 35 × 15 mm
Check device depth against the enclosure door, since deep rail adds 7.5 mm
Match the rail profile and material to the approval list of your ground blocks
Leave room on each strip for end stops, markers and a few spare positions

body.caption: Ground blocks bond to the rail through their metal foot, so check the rail they are approved for.

body.text: Fix the rail to the back plate at regular intervals so it doesn't flex while blocks are wired. Long strips of heavy blocks need fixing points closer together. Cut rail with a rail cutter or a fine saw, deburr the ends, and fit an end stop at both ends of every strip so blocks can't slide along the rail.

body.caption: An end cover and a plug-in jumper: plan these along with the rail length.

body.text: Rail is usually sold in 1 m or 2 m lengths. Include the profile, material, slotted or solid, and length on your order, along with end stops for each strip.

faqs.q: Will terminal blocks from different brands fit the same rail?
faqs.a: Yes, on the same standardized profile. Accessories such as jumpers and end plates are still brand and series specific.

faqs.q: Can I mount 35 mm blocks on a 15 mm rail?
faqs.a: No. Choose blocks designed for the rail profile you are using.
